doe-osti-3002981-near-efficient-and-non-:
Oscar López of Florida Atlantic University, with Arvind Prasadan, Carlos Llosa-Vite, Richard B. Lehoucq, and Daniel M. Dunlavy of Sandia, prove statistical guarantees in report SAND2025-14006R. The subject is multiway inference: drawing conclusions from tensors, data tables with three or more axes. The team works in a Poisson framework for count data, using canonical polyadic decomposition to break a tensor into simpler factors.

Their main result concerns the rank-one case. A rank-limited maximum-likelihood estimator recovers the factors with variance matching the Cramér-Rao lower bound, up to constants and log factors. For higher ranks the estimator can miss that bound, yet estimating the full parameter tensor stays nearly minimax optimal. Computer experiments confirm near-efficiency at rank one and a growing gap at higher ranks, blamed on degeneracy and non-identifiability.
podcast-joerogan-uycEdD5mTiw:
Seeing Earth from space, and what that sight does to a person, is the theme of this Joe Rogan Experience segment. Astronauts call it the overview effect: the sudden feeling that borders are fake and the planet is one fragile home. Rogan has returned to the idea for years.

The talk works through astronaut accounts of weeping at the view of the thin blue line of air. Rogan and his guest weigh why so few people get that sight and what it changes in them. They ask whether leaders should be sent up to see it. A short, awestruck pause in the show's usual noise.
podcast-tuckercarlson-Ai1Gc-N3aIw:
Tucker Carlson explains why trade adviser Peter Navarro is going to jail. Navarro refused a subpoena from the January 6 panel. A court then convicted him of contempt of Congress.

Carlson frames the sentence as punishment for loyalty to Trump. He compares Navarro with officials who faced no such charge. The episode calls him a political prisoner in plain terms. It traces the legal path that led to a cell. Listeners get a defense of a jailed ally, and a charge that the law now bends to serve one party. His allies call the case a warning.
